# Metrics: lifecycle numbers for spoke

Run every command from the repo root. Each command prints the number next to it. The commands use `bun -e` and `git` only.

## DORA keys

Source: `data/deploys.csv` (69 rows, all `service=spoke`) and `data/incidents.csv` (9 rows). Both files are plain CSV: no quotes, no commas inside fields, and the same number of fields on every row.

| Key                            | Value                                                                    | Command                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Deployment frequency, total    | 69 deploys                                                               | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/deploys.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const t=r.map(x=>Date.parse(x[4])).sort((a,b)=>a-b);const w=(t.at(-1)-t[0])/6048e5;console.log(r.length+" deploys, "+w.toFixed(2)+" weeks, "+(r.length/w).toFixed(2)+" per week")'`                               |
| Deployment frequency, per week | 2.68 per week (69 deploys over 25.71 weeks, first to last `deployed_at`) | same command as above                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Lead time for changes          | 66.02 h median, `committed_at` to `deployed_at`, over 69 deploys         | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/deploys.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const h=r.map(x=>(Date.parse(x[4])-Date.parse(x[3]))/36e5).sort((a,b)=>a-b);const n=h.length;console.log("median lead time "+(n%2?h[(n-1)/2]:(h[n/2-1]+h[n/2])/2).toFixed(2)+" h over "+n+" deploys")'`           |
| Change failure rate            | 13.0% (9 of 69 deploys have an `incident_id`)                            | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/deploys.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const f=r.filter(x=>x[5].trim()).length;console.log(f+" of "+r.length+" deploys = "+(

d` names both.                                                 | `bun -e 'const x=c=>require("child_process").execSync(c).toString();const named=new Set([...x("cat work/plan.md").matchAll(/\x60([^\x60]+)\x60/g)].map(m=>m[1]));const files=new Set(x("git log --format= --name-only --grep=^P- 52122d2").split("\n").filter(Boolean));const out=[...files].filter(f=>!named.has(f));console.log(out.length+" outside plan.md, of "+files.size+" files changed by P- commits",out)'`                    |
| Share of commits with the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer | 60.0% (18 of 30 commits)                                                                                                                                       | `bun -e 'const l=require("child_process").execFileSync("git",["log","--format=%h%x09%(trailers:key=Co-Authored-By,valueonly,separator=;)","52122d2"]).toString().trim().split("\n");const c=l.filter(x=>/\tClaude\b/.test(x)).length;console.log(c+" of "+l.length+" commits = "+(100*c/l.length).toFixed(1)+"%")'`                                                                                                                      |
| Median commit size                                         | 16 lines added plus deleted, over 29 commits (skips the root commit `20a20b3`)                                                                                 | `bun -e 'const o=require("child_process").execSync("git log --reverse --format=@%h --numstat 52122d2").toString().split("@").slice(1).map(s=>s.trim().split("\n").slice(1).filter(Boolean).reduce((t,l)=>{const [a,d]=l.split("\t");return t+(a==="-"?0:+a)+(d==="-"?0:+d)},0));const s=o.slice(1).sort((a,b)=>a-b),n=s.length;console.log("median "+(n%2?s[(n-1)/2]:(s[n/2-1]+s[n/2])/2)+" lines over "+n+" commits (first skipped)")'` |

Notes on the git numbers:

- The "P- commits" filter uses `--grep=^P-`, which matches any line of a message. Here it matches only the 3 subjects `P-1`, `P-2` and `P-3`. To check: `git log --format='%h %s' --grep=^P- 52122d2`. The `A-1` commits from the postmortem fix are not P- commits, so they are not counted.
- The range has no binary files, so numstat has no `-` rows to treat as 0.
- 9 of the 29 sized commits change 1 line. They are mostly `approve:` commits that add one row to `work/approvals.jsonl`. These commits pull the median down, so 16 lines describes the mix of commits, not a typical code change.
- The trailer share counts every commit in the range. That includes the root commit and the 11 `approve:` commits, which people made and which have no trailer.

## What these numbers do not prove

**A comparison with DORA.** The change failure rate of 13.0% falls between the "high" (10%) and "medium" (15%) groups in the DORA 2023 State of DevOps report. The "elite" group is at 5%. That ranking holds only if our definition matches DORA's, and it does not quite match. Here a deploy counts as failed only if a row in `incidents.csv` names it. DORA also counts deploys that needed a rollback, hotfix or patch without a formal incident. A rollback with no incident would never appear in this file. So 13.0% is a floor on the true rate. Also, DORA defines its groups from survey answers in ranges, and 9 failures out of 69 is a small sample: one more incident would raise the rate to 14.5%.

**What one feature cannot show.**

- **No comparison.** There is one feature and no baseline. Nothing tells us whether 27.5 h from intent to spec, 0 spec changes after the plan, or 0 files outside the plan is good, typical or lucky. Measuring that needs the same numbers for features built without this workflow, or for many features built with it.
- **The two halves never meet.** The deploy commits in `data/deploys.csv` (for example `de99423` and `afd5991`) do not exist in this repo's history. `deploys.csv` ends on 2026-10-31, before `work/rollout.yaml` was approved on 2026-11-01. This feature's own lead time, failure and restore time are not part of the DORA numbers yet.
- **Following the plan does not mean the result is correct.** "0 files outside plan.md" and "0 spec commits after the plan" show that the process held. They do not show that the code is right. The retried-wrench bug was still shipped and needed a postmortem and the `A-1` fix (`e161f69`, `7dcb13b`). None of the git measures above counts that bug as a failure.
- **A trailer does not show speed or quality.** A 60% trailer share says who is credited on the commits. It says nothing about speed, quality or how much work a person did. METR's 2025 study of experienced open-source developers found that AI tools made them about 19% slower, even though they believed the tools made them faster. Attribution and productivity are different things.
- **Elapsed time includes waiting.** Commit times are author dates, set by whoever made the commit. Intent to spec includes a night and the approval wait (`54cc768`), and it measures elapsed time, not effort.

# Intent: a wrenched bike leaves the feed and reaches the right crew in time

## Problem

We fix 5.46% of wrenched bikes late, so we meet 94.54% against a 95% target. That cost 5,900 pounds in credits in 90 days.
8.94% of wrenched bikes are rented again before a crew reaches them, because the feed still shows them as rentable.

==> work/spec.md <==
# Spec: wrench disables the bike, and the queue sorts by deadline

From the approved `work/intent.md`. Claude Code interviewed the product manager, then wrote this spec.

## Acceptance criteria


==> work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md <==
# 0001: Mark a wrenched bike as disabled in the feed

## Context and Problem Statement

A wrenched bike must stop being rentable at once (AC-1). The GBFS feed gives two ways to do that.


==> work/plan.md <==
# Plan: build the approved spec

Made in plan mode from `work/spec.md`. Claude Code read the code, then wrote this plan. No file changed until it was approved.

## Files that change


==> work/release.md <==
# Release notes: broken bikes leave the map

## Riders

When you report a broken bike, it leaves the map at once. The next rider will not take it by mistake.
Thank you for every report. It helps us fix bikes faster.

==> work/rollout.yaml <==
# How the release reaches riders, one district at a time.
feature_flag: wrench_disables_bike
stages:
  - district: North
  - district: East
  - districts: [Centre, South, West]

==> work/postmortem.md <==
# Postmortem: the double wrench incident in North district

Date of incident: 2026-11-03. All times are UTC.
Sources: `data/incidents/north-double-wrench/` (`incident.log`, `deploys.log`, `chat.txt`, `availability.csv`) and `work/rollout.yaml`.
This postmortem is blameless. It names systems and missing checks, not people.


==> work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md <==
# Intent: two riders wrench the same bike, and the crew gets one job

## Problem

When two different riders wrench the same bike, each report opens its own repair job. Each rider's report has its own `request_id`, so the retry check from postmortem action A-2 does not catch it.
The postmortem shows what duplicate jobs cost. In the North incident, duplicate jobs took 212 bikes out of service, and North availability fell from 97.8% to 89.0%, a drop of 8.8 points. The North crew queue held about 600 jobs against a normal level of about 40.

==> PLAYBOOK.md <==
# Playbook: how we work with Claude Code

## Our AI stance

Claude Code writes drafts: specs, plans, code and tests. People sign. Every stage file is approved by a named person in a set role, and that approval is recorded in `work/approvals.jsonl`. Claude never records an approval itself (`bun run approve` is denied).


==> REVIEW.md <==
# How we review a change

## Bugs

Look for wrong results: a clock that starts at the wrong time, a queue in the wrong order, a feed that lags.


==> work/review.md <==
# Review of the build

The reviewer subagent read the branch against `work/spec.md`, `work/plan.md` and `REVIEW.md`.

## Findings


==> work/findings.md <==
# Findings: why wrenched bikes miss the 48 hour limit

Claude Code read `data/wrenches.csv` and `data/repairs.csv`: 90 days, 2,160 wrench reports.

# The chain: from intent to playbook

This file follows one feature for spoke, Kestrel's bike-share service, from the first problem statement to the team playbook that came out of it. The feature makes a wrenched (reported broken) bike leave the public feed and reach the right repair crew within 48 hours. The rule behind it: Claude Code writes each draft, and a named person in a set role signs it. Each signature is one row in `work/approvals.jsonl`, holding the file path, its SHA-256 hash, the signer's role and name, and a timestamp. Every stage starts from the approved file of the stage before.

## The stages

**1. Intent: `work/intent.md`.** States the problem: 5.46% of wrenched bikes are fixed late, against a 95% on-time target, and 8.94% are rented again before a crew reaches them. Signed by Theo Lindqvist (pm) on 2026-10-27T14:00:00Z.

**2. Spec: `work/spec.md`.** Claude Code interviewed the product manager and turned the intent into acceptance criteria: a wrench disables the bike, and the crew queue sorts by deadline. Signed by Theo Lindqvist (pm) on 2026-10-28T16:00:00Z.

**3. Decision: `work/decisions/0001-disable-in-feed.md`.** Chooses how the GBFS feed marks a wrenched bike as disabled (AC-1). Signed by Ines Moreau (tech-lead) on 2026-10-29T10:30:00Z.

**4. Plan: `work/plan.md`.** Written in plan mode from the spec, listing the files that change. Nothing was edited before approval. Signed by Ines Moreau (tech-lead) on 2026-10-29T14:00:00Z.

**5. Acceptance tests: `test/acceptance/`.** One test file per acceptance criterion (AC-1 to AC-4), plus a helper. After this approval nobody may change these files, so the code has to change instead. Signed by Raj Patel (qa) on 2026-10-30T10:00:00Z.

**6. Review rules: `REVIEW.md`.** What a reviewer looks for, such as a clock that starts at the wrong time or a queue in the wrong order. Signed by Ines Moreau (tech-lead) on 2026-10-31T10:00:00Z. The reviewer subagent's report, `work/review.md`, has no row in the log.

**7. Release notes: `work/release.md`.** What riders and crews are told. Signed by Theo Lindqvist (pm) on 2026-11-01T11:00:00Z.

**8. Rollout: `work/rollout.yaml`.** Turns on the feature flag `wrench_disables_bike` one district at a time: North, then East, then Centre, South and West. Nobody may deploy to production until this file is approved. Signed by Mei Tanaka (release-manager) on 2026-11-01T15:00:00Z.

**9. Postmortem: `work/postmortem.md`.** On 2026-11-03 the rider app's retries of `POST /wrench` opened duplicate jobs in North, the first rollout district. The postmortem is blameless and led to the `A-1` fix. Signed by Ines Moreau (tech-lead) on 2026-11-04T11:00:00Z.

**10. Next intent: `work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md`.** A follow-up problem from the postmortem: two different riders wrench the same bike and get two jobs. This starts the next chain. Signed by Theo Lindqvist (pm) on 2026-11-04T13:30:00Z.

**11. Playbook: `PLAYBOOK.md`.** Writes down how the team works with Claude Code. Signed by Dana Okafor (em) on 2026-11-05T11:00:00Z.

On 2026-11-13 the SHA-256 of each of the ten signed single files matched the hash in its approval row, so none of them has changed since it was signed. `test/acceptance/` is a directory, and that check did not cover it. `work/findings.md`, the data analysis behind the intent, has no approval row.

## Three numbers

From `work/metrics.md`, quoted exactly:

- Change failure rate: "13.0% (9 of 69 deploys have an `incident_id`)"
- Lead time for changes: "66.02 h median, `committed_at` to `deployed_at`, over 69 deploys"
- Share of commits with the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer: "60.0% (18 of 30 commits)"

These numbers do not prove that this workflow made spoke faster, safer or more correct: there is no baseline to compare against, the deploy data ends before this feature's rollout was approved, and the double-wrench bug shipped anyway.

## How to check

- To see who signed what, read `work/approvals.jsonl`. It has one JSON row per approval, in time order.
- To check that a file has not changed since it was signed, run `sha256sum <file>` and compare the result with the row's `sha256`.
- `work/metrics.md` lists the command behind each number. Run them from the repo root.
